          FotMob Premier League Team of the Month: Evanilson, Rice and Jackson Stand Out With October Performances
        
      
                          
                      Nov 3, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Bournemouth forward Evanilson secured the highest average FotMob player rating for his performances across October in the Premier League, while Declan Rice and Nicolas Jackson also made the XI following impressive displays.

Another month of Premier League action has passed, but who impressed the most? Well, luckily, we have FotMob’s player ratings to answer that exact question.Using those ratings, we've assembled our Premier League Team of the Month, with Opta data providing a deeper look at the performances behind the ratings.

Following an extended international break, Premier League action resumed on 10 October after two weekends off. Four matchdays have been played since, ending with Everton’s trip to face Newcastle on 2 November. This team picks out the highest performers between those dates.
Bart Verbruggen kept three clean sheets across his four Premier League appearances in October – no goalkeeper in the competition collected more.

The last of those came in an exceptional 1-0 win at Manchester City on 31 October, helping Brighton secure their first-ever competitive win away at City at the 18th attempt. That match saw Verbruggen make seven saves at the Etihad Stadium; only one goalkeeper made more in a Premier League game between our eligible dates (Senne Lammens vs Chelsea – 8).
Overall, the Dutch goalkeeper saved 14 of the 15 shots on target he faced in the month, with his saves giving him a goals prevented value of 1.9 (one goal conceded from an xGOT of 2.9).
Andy Robertson has enjoyed a successful month of Premier League action for Tottenham, winning all three games that he’s featured in for the club.

Robertson’s three Premier League appearances in October saw him secure a FotMob player rating of 7.0 or above in all three games. That’s the first time he’s managed that in three successive Premier League matches since doing so in December 2024 for Liverpool.

Only Mohammed Kudus (16) fired in more open-play crosses for Spurs across the month than the Scottish defender (13), while he also created five chances and assisted one of their goals in the 3-1 win over Coventry on 19 October.
Ezri Konsa played in all four of Arsenal’s games between the beginning of October and 2 November, and ended on the winning side in each one.

The England defender even scored his first Premier League goal for Arsenal and his first in the competition since May 2025, in their 2-0 victory over Everton on 24 October. His FotMob player rating of 8.0 in that win was his highest in a Premier League game in nearly a year (8.0 on 30 November 2025 for Aston Villa vs Wolves).

Forming a formidable partnership with Gabriel Magalhães, the Gunners conceded just one goal in their four games across the period considered, while they allowed opponents a league-low 10 shots on target worth just 3.2 xG.
He only just edged out his central defensive partner in this team, with the Brazilian ranking below Konsa and Van Hecke with an average monthly rating of 7.7.

Jan Paul van Hecke ended October with a Player of the Match performance in Spurs’ 2-0 home win over 10-man Crystal Palace on 31 October. He scored the second goal in that victory, meaning he’s now already halfway (2) to the total Premier League goal tally he achieved over four seasons at Brighton (4).

A reliable player when building possession from the back, Van Hecke attempted (419) and completed (373) the most passes among Premier League players in October. He also ranked in the top 10 for duel success (63.6%) among the 99 players involved in 30+ duels across the month.

Ben White grabbed an assist in two of his three Premier League appearances in October, creating goals in the wins over Leeds and Everton. The Englishman already has as many Premier League assists this season (3) as he did in 2025-26 (1) and 2024-25 (2) combined.

Both of those performances saw him achieve impressive FotMob player ratings (7.8 vs Leeds, 8.1 vs Everton) and, together with a 6.8 rating in the away win at Nottingham Forest between those two games at the Emirates, White ended the month as the fourth highest-scoring defender (7.6).
Jérémy Doku scored in Man City’s opening game of October in the 3-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield, and then set up another in his second game against Ipswich Town.

He may have ended on the losing side in his last two games for City in the month, but he was a constant threat to opponents Aston Villa and Brighton; he was involved in more shots than any other City player across those matches (12 – six shots, six chances created).

Across the entire league in October, no player was involved in more shots following a ball carry than Doku (10 – five shots, five chances created) and he topped the league rankings for take-ons both overall (48) and in the opposition half (41).
